construct: HFE dysfunction impairs hepatocyte upregulation of hepcidin. Hepcidin normally binds ferroportin and promotes its internalization and degradation. Low hepcidin therefore leaves more active ferroportin on enterocytes and reticuloendothelial cells, increasing intestinal iron absorption and iron release into plasma.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: HFE C282Y homozygosity with elevated transferrin saturation, ferritin, liver disease, hyperpigmentation, and diabetes identifies HFE hemochromatosis driven by inadequate hepcidin signaling.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Reduced apical iron uptake or reduced ferroportin activity would decrease systemic iron delivery and therefore cannot produce this iron-loading phenotype.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Low hepcidin fails to trigger ferroportin internalization/degradation, so increased ferroportin activity is the uniquely directionally correct mechanism.
